_comment: Semantic versions for the hand-written player-facing content that documents
THE RULE (owner, 2026-09-08): the site, the booklet and the load cards show
THE GAME AS WE WANT IT PLAYED, not as the build behaves. When they differ,
the difference is RECORDED AND ROUTED TO ARC as game work. Never close the
gap by editing the site to match the build.
The separation is the point. Quinn defines the game as intended and finds
where the build departs from it; App renders and documents it the same way.
If either side quietly rewrites itself to match whatever the build does, the
difference stops being visible to anyone and the build silently becomes the
spec. Two lists keep both directions visible:
aheadOfLive - documented, the game has not caught up. Split by whether it
is BUILT and waiting on a promote, or not built at all — they
clear by different means and only the second is owed work.
divergences - the site is right and the BUILD is wrong. These are bug
reports for Arc, not corrections to make here.
the game: the instruction booklet and the /play load-screen cards.
WHAT THIS CONTENT TARGETS (owner, 2026-09-08): the EPISODE ONE DESIGN — the
game as it is meant to behave — NOT the build that happens to be deployed.
The booklet is closer to a spec than to release notes, and the game catches up
to it. This may change once Episode One is finished; for now the design is the
target.
That inverts the staleness question. The useful signal is not 'is the manual
behind the game' but 'what has the game not caught up with yet' — which is a
known, temporary, expected state, and a to-do for the game rather than a
defect in the book. aheadOfLive is that list.
It also means a documented behaviour that is not live is CORRECT, not wrong.
The trap it creates is the opposite one: finding the game doing something the
booklet does not say and 'fixing' the booklet to match. Arc flagged exactly
that with the Health Relic — its +25% maxHP does nothing on equip today, and
the booklet would have been wrong to describe the bug. Check whether a
difference is a game defect before treating it as a documentation error.
WHY SEMVER AND NOT A GIT SHA: a hash tells you which build shipped, but two
hashes cannot be compared — you cannot look at ec589de and 146964d and say
which is newer. Version numbers sort.
SCOPE (owner, 2026-09-08): the booklet teaches SYSTEMS and rules. Per-skill
mechanical detail — radius, self-heal, what a named enemy skill does — belongs
in /walkthrough/, not here. The booklet names Poison Cloud in the bestiary and
does not say what it does; that is correct, not a gap. The test is whether it
is a RULE needed to understand the game, or a FACT about one skill or enemy.
BUMP RULES (version):
major - restructured (chapters added/removed/reordered)
minor - a mechanic's description changed, or content was added
patch - wording, typos, a figure swap; nothing a player learns differently
reviewed  - when a person last read this against the design.
history   - append-only; the game version at each content version, which
answers 'what was the game when the manual was X'. Newest first.

history.note: No prose change. Records which ahead-of-live items are built-and-waiting versus not-built, and opens a game-defects list for places the booklet is right and the build is wrong.

Charging stated as a two-sided gamble: what the charging unit spends, what breaking it costs them, what landing it costs you, and that committing to break a charge puts you in reach of the rest of the room. Stagger bar documented as a readout of damage still required; Scan now says it names the exact figure.

Retargeted at the Episode One design rather than the deployed build. Interrupt now costs the whole turn; statuses tick at end of turn (which removes the last-stack-acts-free behaviour entirely); the winding-up hint now states the payoff.

Initiative trigger corrected, turn economy added, status-stacking model rewritten, combat log expanded with its figure, controller + battle speed added, Mother Slime reach 1→2, auto-save indicator, Cure vs Mugwort.
Pre-review baseline: the booklet as it stood when the 0.8.2592 delta review began. Recorded retrospectively; earlier history predates versioning.

aheadOfLive.item: Interrupt applies Stunned — the creature loses its next turn, not just its reactions
Statuses tick and decrement at the END of the affected unit's turn (was the start)
aheadOfLive.note: Verified live by Quinn on 2615: the stack is still on the unit while it acts and only ticks at end of turn, so the old last-stack-acts-free window is genuinely gone.

aheadOfLive.item: Status stacks make the same status easier to land again (QB-116)
A landed charged attack hits far harder than an ordinary one
aheadOfLive.state: not built — owed by the game
aheadOfLive.note: Design intent only; charge damage untouched as of 2616. Clears when the balance retune lands.

history.note: Winding-up card names both sides of the trade and points at Scan.
Winding-up-enemy card now states the payoff (a free turn) rather than arguing from what retreating costs.

Rewritten as short snippets from the booklet's Hints chapter. AP removed — it had been retired from the game while three cards still taught it. Cut to Episode One content. Cure corrected against Mugwort.

aheadOfLive.item: Breaking a charge costs the enemy its next turn

divergences.item: Health relic: the booklet says it increases total HP (design: +25% maxHP). It does nothing on equip today.
divergences.note: Arc, 2026-09-08. Do NOT reword the booklet to match; the fix rides the balance retune.
